newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips close up, 2nd board tumbles.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips close up, 2nd board tumbles.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks closed higher in thin trading on Monday, while small-capitalised stocks were down sharply.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 leading stocks closed up 4.59 points to 1177.07, while the Second Board index was down 12.10 points, or 1.9 percent, to 622.41.
"It's been very quiet except for Tenaga which was traded quite heavily," said a local institutional dealer. Tenaga was up 50 cents to 10.80 ringgit with 8.9 million shares traded.
"The (Composite) index has been pulled up by Tenaga," said an institutional dealer in Singapore.
"The Second Board came down today just as I had expected it to," said the local dealer.
U.S. institutional funds had been very quiet in the run-up to the U.S. elections on Tuesday, dealers said.

"U.S. funds are staying out of the market until the elections are over, and the Japanese have been on holiday today so there is very little foreign interest in our market today," said the local dealer.
Volume stood at 223 million shares traded, valued at 1.95 billion ringgit. Losers dominated gainers by 442 to 132.
